AlignmentCondition.description:
Unsafe when a variable strays from a target variable by ``tolerance`` or more.

For example a beam position compared against its reference setpoint.

kind.description: Condition type. 'alignment' compares a variable with a target variable.
kind.title: Kind

target_device.description: Device carrying the target variable (default: the same device).
target_device.title: Target Device

tolerance.description: UNSAFE when |value - target| is this large or larger (in the variable's units).
tolerance.title: Tolerance

hysteresis.description: How much closer than the tolerance the value must come before the interlock counts as safe again.
hysteresis.title: Hysteresis

AlignmentCondition.title: AlignmentCondition

ConfigChangeCondition.description:
Unsafe when device settings change from the values they had when armed.

An operator arms it on the interlock server once the settings are
right; until then it is unsafe. Any later change to one of
the variables trips it until it is re-armed.

kind.description: Condition type. 'config_change' trips when settings move from their armed values.
kind.title: Kind

ConfigChangeCondition.title: ConfigChangeCondition

ExternalCondition.description:
Unsafe while an external program says so over UDP.

For a program outside GEECS — a motion controller on another computer,
say — that sends one short text packet to the interlock server whenever
its state changes. The whole text is searched, in any case, for whole
words: ``warning`` or ``unsafe`` anywhere makes the condition unsafe;
otherwise ``safe`` anywhere (``stage1 safe``) makes it safe, unless a
negation stands right next to it (``not safe``, ``safe: false``). Any
other packet makes the signal unknown, which is unsafe until a
recognised packet arrives; so is the time before the first packet.

kind.description: Condition type. 'external' follows UDP status packets.
kind.title: Kind

port.description: UDP port the interlock server listens on for this signal. Conditions naming the same port share one signal.
port.title: Port

source.description: Optional name of the sending program, shown to operators.
source.title: Source

sender.description: The sending computer's IPv4 address. When set, a packet from any other address is unrecognised (unsafe): no other host can clear the signal. Leave empty to accept any sender.
sender.title: Sender

max_age_s.description: Seconds without a packet before the signal counts as lost. Leave empty when the sender transmits only on a change (silence is normal).
max_age_s.title: Max Age S

ExternalCondition.title: ExternalCondition

Interlock.description: One interlock: a name and the conditions that make it unsafe (any one is enough).

name.description: Short name shown to operators and on the status stream.
name.title: Name

description.description: Optional note on what this interlock protects.
description.title: Description

enabled.description: Set false to keep the entry without arming it (shown as not armed, never counted in the verdict).
enabled.title: Enabled

conditions.description: The conditions watched; the interlock is unsafe while any one of them is. List several to report them under one name.
conditions.title: Conditions

settle_s.description: Seconds every condition must stay safe after a trip before the interlock reports OK again.
settle_s.title: Settle S

Interlock.title: Interlock

StaleCondition.description:
Unsafe when a device stops publishing.

Always unsafe while the device's subscription is disconnected.  With
``max_age_s`` it is also unsafe when no new update has arrived from the
device for that long — only meaningful for a free-running device that
keeps publishing between shots.

kind.description: Condition type. 'stale' trips when a device stops publishing.
kind.title: Kind

max_age_s.description: Seconds without a new update before the device counts as stale. Leave empty to trip only on a disconnect.
max_age_s.title: Max Age S

StaleCondition.title: StaleCondition

ThresholdCondition.description:
Unsafe when a variable crosses a limit.

For example ``operator: '>'`` with ``limit: 4094`` trips when a camera's
``MaxCounts`` saturates. ``==`` and ``!=`` are for status codes and
other whole numbers: ``operator: '!='`` with ``limit: 0`` trips on any
nonzero fault code.

kind.description: Condition type. 'threshold' compares one variable to a limit.
kind.title: Kind

operator.description: The reading is UNSAFE when 'value <operator> limit' holds, e.g. '>' trips above the limit.
operator.title: Operator

limit.description: The limit the reading is compared against.
limit.title: Limit

hysteresis.description: How far back past the limit the reading must come before the interlock counts as safe again (0 = resume as soon as it is back).
hysteresis.title: Hysteresis

ThresholdCondition.title: ThresholdCondition

description:
The experiment's software interlocks, watched by the interlock server.

Notes
-----
One named configuration, stored as ``interlocks/<name>.yaml`` in the
experiment's scanner configs.  The interlock server reads it at start
and on a reload; an edit takes effect at the next one.

schema_version.description: Format version of this config file. Leave at 1 — tools update this automatically when the file format changes.
schema_version.title: Schema Version

stale_after_s.description: Seconds without an update from a device before every interlock reading it trips. Leave empty for devices that publish only on a change (a disconnect still trips).
stale_after_s.title: Stale After S

title: InterlockSet
